noah (Eng): Quick offboarding question- my last day will be 2029-03-31. I have a 401(k) loan and an HSA payroll election. What's the timeline for rolling the 401(k) to an IRA vs moving to a new employer plan? Also: will the loan auto-offset at termination or is there a grace period? Finally, how do I stop HSA pre-tax deductions on the final paycheck?

taylor-peopleops: Congrats on the new gig! Short answers: you can roll to an IRA or to a new employer's plan (if the new plan accepts rollovers). Loan behavior depends on plan rules; many plans treat termination as a triggering event after which outstanding loans may be deemed distributions and taxed unless repaid or rolled per plan rules.

katie-401k-admin: From admin side: we notify Sequoia (our TPA) at separation. We typically have a 60-day window where participants can arrange repayment/rollover before a loan offset is processed, but that depends on the plan document and loan terms. If you want to avoid offset, options are: repay in full before last paycheck, roll remaining vested balance into an IRA (note: loans typically can't be rolled; outstanding loan may still be taxable), or arrange with Sequoia for repayment elections if allowed.

ben-payroll: HSA stop: set HSA deferral to 0% in Workday before the final payroll cutoff (17:00 PT two business days before the run). If you miss that cutoff and we deduct after termination, payroll will reverse on the next cycle and coordinate with HSA vendor. Ping payroll if your last paycheck timing is tight.

marta (Sequoia Plan Services): Hey Noah  Sequoia here. Key notes:
- Loan offset timing varies by plan; ours allows a documented 60-day cure period post-termination for active efforts to repay or arrange a rollover of eligible account balances.
- Outstanding loans are not eligible for rollover; if offset occurs, the offset amount is taxable and reported on Form 1099-R.
- We can discuss options: in-plan repayment, cash repayment, or voluntary pre-termination payoff. Email retirements@sequoia.com with Subject: "Separation - Noah L - loan review" and include last 4 SSN + loan ID.

noah (Eng): If I roll the vested balance to an IRA, will that preserve pretax status even if there's an outstanding loan that gets offset?

katie-401k-admin: Rolling the vested balance preserves pretax status for the rolled portion. But any loan offset that is treated as a distribution becomes taxable and won't be part of the rollover. So partial outcomes are possible: rolled funds preserve tax deferral; offset portion is taxable.

noah (Eng): Any deadlines I should be mindful of for paperwork to avoid the offset?

marta (Sequoia Plan Services): Submit documentation as soon as separation is known. Best practice: 1) notify benefits@redwood.com of termination date, 2) email retirements@sequoia.com with loan info + intent (repay vs explore options), 3) if you plan to roll to an IRA, open the IRA in advance and get the rollover wiring instructions. We generally send a loan cure notice and work with employer to delay offset while cure efforts are underway.

benefits-bot: Reminder: final payroll cutoff is 17:00 PT two business days before pay run. HSA deferral changes: https://intranet.redwood/hr/hsa-fsa. 401(k) rollover resources: https://intranet.redwood/hr/401k-rollover

ben-payroll: One more practical tip: if your final pay includes accrued PTO, deferrals may apply depending on payroll timing. If you want zero deferrals on final pay, make sure Workday change is processed early and confirm with payroll.

noah (Eng): Thanks folks. I'll notify people-ops and open an IRA so we have the instructions. Would appreciate a brief call with Sequoia if anything is unclear.

taylor-peopleops: Happy to set that up  we'll coordinate calendar with Sequoia and payroll. Thanks!
